title: Conservation of Retrotransposon Fragments in Animal Genomes
content: Long terminal repeats (LTRs) of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) contain transcription factor (TF)-binding motifs involved in interactions between ERVs and the host genome. We analyzed two LTR fragments from bovine placenta-expressed betaretroviruses, BERVK1 and BERV-beta3, to identify factors contributing to their sequence conservation across three distantly related species: Bos taurus, Oryctolagus cuniculus, and Apis cerana. Both fragments contain GGAGA, a noncanonical binding motif of the ETS-family transcription factor PU.1. Homologous sequences were identified in protein-coding genes, predominantly those associated with cytoskeletal remodeling, cell adhesion, and intercellular interactions. In several cases, these sequences occurred within conserved protein domains. Homologous sequences were also found in piRNAs involved in suppression of ERV activity, miRNA precursors in cattle and honey bees, and lncRNAs. Several factors may therefore contribute to the sequence conservation of K1 and beta3 fragments, including exaptation of ERV fragments, host regulatory motifs, localization within conserved domains of protein-coding genes, and a balance between TF binding and inhibition of ERV transcription. Multiple potential sources of conservation may provide a basis for more targeted genotyping by combining a conserved ERV LTR fragment with a protein-coding gene fragment from a specific functional module.
